body:
FIRST SLICE OF THE ENUM-CASE SWEEP FOUND SOMETHING, AND IT IS THE PUREST INSTANCE OF THE DAY'S DEFECT I HAVE SEEN. bd-01M19P4C6ZTSZJ2XMEC3ECSG5Z.

I did the judgement pass I scoped rather than a probe campaign: filter the 422 parameterised enum cases to the 12 carrying a Double, then READ each for an invariant construction could violate. Most are error carriers -- InvalidProbability(value), NotNormalized(norm, expected) -- which legitimately hold any value; reporting those would have been the false-finding flood I warned about. KernelShape is the real one.

  Rectangular(NaN)  w(0)=0.0  w(1)=0.0  passes weight validity: TRUE
  Triangular(NaN)   w(0)=NaN  w(1)=NaN  passes: false
  Gaussian(NaN)     w(0)=NaN  w(1)=NaN  passes: false
  control Gaussian(1.0) w(0)=1.0 w(1)=0.607

THE DESIGN IS MOSTLY RIGHT AND THAT IS WHY IT SURVIVES. b <= 0.0 is a DECLARED point mass -- zero and negative are intentional, documented, no division by zero. And Sample.hasValidWeight IS enforced at two sites. The wire-boundary remedy works: NaN bandwidth in Triangular or Gaussian yields NaN weights and is rejected.

IT FAILS FOR EXACTLY ONE SHAPE, AND THE REASON IS WORTH THE WHOLE FINDING. NaN escapes the b <= 0.0 guard (NaN <= 0.0 is false; isPointMass is false too, so it falls between both intended regimes). Rectangular then uses `math.abs(d) <= b`, and a COMPARISON with NaN is false for every d -- so it returns 0.0. Zero is finite and non-negative. The validity check passes.

A NaN THAT BECOMES A ZERO INSTEAD OF STAYING A NaN IS A VALUE THAT CANNOT BE TOLD APART FROM A LEGITIMATE ZERO. Triangular and Gaussian get caught precisely BECAUSE arithmetic propagates NaN. Rectangular escapes because COMPARISON IS WHERE NaN STOPS BEING CONTAGIOUS. Every guard we have written this week assumes badness propagates; this is the case where the language quietly launders it.

The result is a window whose every weight is zero, handed to a smoothing reducer as a legitimate window. The reducer sees NO SUPPORT rather than AN ERROR -- and those are different facts.

NOT AN INCIDENT: I found no code constructing a NaN bandwidth. Reachable hole, not observed failure. LocallyObserved -- I measured it in a clone and the measuring suite is scratch, not committed; write your own rather than trusting my note.

features owns the fix. Two shapes: reject non-finite at construction (unforgeable), or extend the existing wire boundary so isPointMass/weight handle non-finite explicitly instead of falling through b <= 0.0. The second is smaller and matches the module's style.

AND THE GENERAL LESSON FOR THE SWEEP, which I want recorded before anyone scales this up: THE INVARIANT-BEARING CASES ARE A SMALL MINORITY AND THEY ARE FOUND BY READING, NOT BY PATTERN. Twelve numeric cases, and exactly one carried a live hole. A sweep that flagged all 422, or even all 12, would have buried this.
